Sterdyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sterdyń, Poland

Not demolished. Sterdyń, with medieval roots, likely gained town rights in 1737, later becoming a private village under the Kiszka, Ossoliński, and Krasiński families from 1869. Jewish settlement's founding is unknown, though an 1864 census recorded about 200 Jews (6.7% of 3,002 residents); a wooden synagogue built in 1870 burned down in 1915. A 1941 ghetto held about 1,000 people by 1942, including Soviet POWs; on September 23, 1942, 300-400 were murdered on the ghetto grounds, with remaining residents deported to Treblinka. In February 1943, Germans killed 11 local Poles for supporting hidden Jews. This cemetery, likely established in the second half of the 19th century, holds execution-victim mass graves, though its wartime history is otherwise undocumented.
